Video Has No Sound? Check the Audio Track

Choose the saved video to check whether it has no audio track, an audio track whose decoded samples are all zero, or an audio signal. The file stays in your browser. Check the same moment in your editor to decide whether to re-export or fix playback.

Check audio in an MP4, MOV or WebM

Choose an MP4, MOV or WebM video.

The check reads up to 60 seconds from your chosen start time when there is one decodable audio track. Use a later time to check a quiet section. If the file has multiple tracks, select and listen to them separately in a desktop video player or editor.

What did the audio check find?

Check the exportCheck the timelineCheck playbackCheck the file

No audio track was found

Go back to the source or editor project. Preview the sound on the expected timeline and make sure the track overlaps the exported segment. In Canva, select Share → Download → MP4 Video and check which pages you are exporting. Download again and check that the new MP4 has an audio track. Some Canva AI clips are generated without sound. Check the route you chose in the Canva AI video guide.

If the source has no track, add the original audio or a replacement in your editor. A format conversion cannot recreate missing sound.

An audio track exists, but the decoded samples are zero

Check a later start time if the soundtrack starts after the scan window. If the section that should contain sound is still zero, compare it with the editor preview at the same time. Unmute the clip or audio track, raise its track volume if it was set to zero, and make sure it spans the exported part. In Canva, see the track and clip volume controls.

Export a fresh MP4 and check the same time range again. A zero result covers the decoded samples in the reported time window. Blank sections between samples and sections outside the window are separate checks.

There is an audio signal, but playback sounds silent

Listen to the checked section in another player. Unmute the player, confirm the output device and use a track selector if available. The peak indicates the strongest digital sample in the scan. Encoding can leave a tiny nonzero signal in a quiet section. The tool groups peaks below −120 dBFS as very low. Listen to confirm whether dialogue, music or other expected sound is present.

If another player can hear the file, check the first app’s audio format support. Test a compatible copy with the local video converter and keep the original. To inspect the audio separately, extract the soundtrack as WAV from a supported single-track file.

The audio check could not finish

Try the known tone file below. If that works, check the original file in a desktop player. Look for multiple tracks, an unsupported codec or an incomplete download. If the first scan ended before the sound should begin, enter that time in seconds and check again.

If the tone file also fails, try a current desktop browser with audio decoding support. Compare the same complete file in a desktop player before changing the export.

Compare three known MP4 files

  • MP4 with no audio track. The checker should report no audio track.
  • MP4 with one silent AAC track. The decoded samples should all be zero.
  • MP4 with one AAC track and a test tone. The checker should detect a signal. Start playback at low volume.

These files were created as test media. Check Canva’s MP4 export instructions for how audio is included in the exported pages.
